partners.mechanism_chain: PIGA (HGNC:9019) —DISRUPTS→ GPI-anchored protein biosynthesis; PIGT (HGNC:14938) —DISRUPTS→ GPI-anchored protein biosynthesis; GPI-anchored protein biosynthesis —LEADS_TO→ Hemolytic anemia (HP:0001883); GPI-anchored protein biosynthesis —LEADS_TO→ Thrombosis (HP:0001927); GPI-anchored protein biosynthesis —LEADS_TO→ Bone marrow failure (HP:0005571). Mutations in PIGA (for PNH) and PIGT (for PNH2) lead to a defect in the shared pathway of GPI-anchored protein biosynthesis. This deficiency results in the absence of GPI-anchored proteins (like CD55 and CD59) on the cell surface, leading to complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis, thrombosis, and bone marrow failure, characteristic of both PNH and PNH2.

raw.translational: Understanding the shared pathway defect in GPI anchor synthesis between PNH and GPIBD21 could inform therapeutic strategies. For PNH, complement inhibitors are effective; exploring similar complement-modulating approaches or strategies to restore GPI anchor function in specific cell types might be relevant for GPIBD21, particularly for mitigating hemolytic crises if present.
